Neco Williams thumped it at Bruno Guimarães, who went down and stayed down. The Forest support were unhappy at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. “Are you City in disguise?” they chanted.View image in fullscreenNoni Madueke fires home – via a deflection – the only goal of the game.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianCould a set piece provide the breakthrough? It felt the likeliest route. Murillo headed wide from a Forest corner in the 20th minute and was bloodied into the bargain; there was a whistle for a foul in the mass of bodies inside the six-yard box. At the other end, Kai Havertz headed over from a Rice free-kick on 37 minutes. He had a good look at the ball and was well-placed. It was a decent chance.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionArsenal have been a little barren in the first half this season. This was the seventh time in 10 matches since the Community Shield that they had failed to score in one. It has not been a problem. They needed to raise their levels for the second half.Arteta’s first change was Madueke for Eberechi Eze on the left wing; an admission that the latter had failed to exert an influence. There was also a triple substitution on 66 minutes, the manager sending on Jurriën Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyökeres for Ben White, Guimarães and Havertz. He needed to shake things up because nothing was happening for his team. It was Forest who pushed after the restart, with Delap continuing to put himself about. He asked questions of Gabriel Magalhães, albeit the Arsenal defender tended to have the answers.The minutes ticked down, the contest narrowing to a fine point and we waited to see whether there could be a moment, one big chance. Martin Ødegaard almost provided it in the 72nd minute when he released Timber with a lovely pass up the inside right. When he pulled back, Rice lifted wastefully high.Glasner’s decision to introduce Ibrahim Sangaré for Dan Ndoye shortly afterwards was telling. Sangaré’s mission was to bolster the Forest midfield and yet he was slow to react to a half-cleared ball. When Rice played the pass, Madueke took over.“We showed a champion spirit,” Madueke said. “Maybe last season, this game might not have gone for us. We have the extra belief and mentality.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueNottingham ForestArsenalmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace  | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Brighton scored three times in the first 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez from 51 metres, and then piled on more misery as they beat Crystal Palace 5-0
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Brighton scored three times in the first 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez from 51 metres, and then piled on more misery as they beat Crystal Palace 5-0
Content: Crystal Palace's Walter Benítez sticks out a flailing arm in vain as Diego Gómez’s audacious halfway-line shot puts Brighton 2-0 up.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCrystal Palace's Walter Benítez sticks out a flailing arm in vain as Diego Gómez’s audacious halfway-line shot puts Brighton 2-0 up.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueGómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal PalaceEd Aaronsat the Amex StadiumSun 18 Oct 2026 11.06 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.Leeds United 1-1 Manchester United: Premier League – live reactionRead moreThe concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February afterPalace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.View image in fullscreenYasin Ayari’s deflected effort results in Brighton’s third goal.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez.The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThings got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood scoring from close range six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBrighton & Hove AlbionCrystal Palacematch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Marcus Tavernier opened the scoring in the sixth minute as Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 to secure their first Premier League win of the season
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Marcus Tavernier opened the scoring in the sixth minute as Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 to secure their first Premier League win of the season
Content: Evanilson doubles Bournemouth’s lead after taking the ball past the Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEvanilson doubles Bournemouth’s lead after taking the ball past the Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueEvanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man SunderlandJohn Brewinat the Vitality StadiumSun 18 Oct 2026 11.19 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for aPremier Leaguewin is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity,Sunderlandwere sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on CarrickRead moreThere was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched and their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.Both teams had made five changes from Thursday andBournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”Granit Xhaka’s early stumble prefaced a jet-lagged, error-strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away game since 1973. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home. “I was waiting for him to shoot but he can see more than you and me,” Rose said.“Exactly the situation we wanted to avoid,” Le Bris said, and Danso’s exit swiftly made things worse. Evanilson again escaped beyond a dallying defender exposed by Alderete ducking away from the ball. Clumsiness served as no defence. Craig Pawson, the referee, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel.View image in fullscreenMarcus Tavernier points the way after scoring Bournemouth’s first goal.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersBeing a goal and a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First‑half chances piled up, Robin Roefs repeatedly asked to bail out bungling defenders. “If you have one player more you have to use the momentum,” Rose said.With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris can only fight with the players available. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal following injury on international duty, was missing altogether from the matchday squad. “We decided not to rush the process,” Le Bris said. Timur Tutierov, loaned last season to Exeter, chased autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution on 59 minutes.On the sidelines Rose, who revealed last week that he had binge‑watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball. His need for three points was implicit. With the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands, relegation battles cannot be countenanced. The second goal was accompanied by a collective sigh of relief, arriving via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, assisted by Alderete’s brain-fog backpass, supplied a hip swivel of which Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud, sitting Roefs down to slot into an empty net. “I am happy that he rewarded himself with a goal,” Rose said of his No 9. “He is always working hard for the team.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenKevin Danso brings down Evanilson before being shown a red card by referee Craig Pawson.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersBournemouth signed off with 29 shots. If thoughts understandably drifted to Thursday and Milan, seven-time European champions, coming to Dorset, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted. Though Sunderland enjoyed a late, brief spell of pressure, Bournemouth calmly collected a win that capped a historic week in club history. “It felt very clear, after [the 5-1 defeat on Friday against] Chelsea we were waiting for this game,” Rose said. “I am settling in well, I love the region. It’s a pleasure to work here. Everyone here stays patient and I really appreciate it.”For Le Bris, any European success will only be a sticking plaster. “It’s hard to fix without a specific pattern,” he said, lamenting many mistakes. “It wasn’t the best version of Sunderland.”Two clubs facing similar challenges appear on different trajectories.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBournemouthSunderlandmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Northampton break England’s duck in Champions Cup with victory over Cardiff | Champions Cup | The Guardian
description: Northampton survived a sizeable scare from Cardiff to put one on the board for the Prem in the Champions Cup with a 28-12 victory
Author: Gerard Meagher
Headline: Northampton survived a sizeable scare from Cardiff to put one on the board for the Prem in the Champions Cup with a 28-12 victory
Content: George Hendy celebrates after touching down to score for Northampton.Photograph: David Davies/PAView image in fullscreenGeorge Hendy celebrates after touching down to score for Northampton.Photograph: David Davies/PAChampions CupNorthampton break England’s duck in Champions Cup with victory over CardiffPool 4: Northampton 28-12 CardiffSaints claim first win for Prem side at eighth time of askingGerard Meagherat DPD Stadium at Franklin's GardensSun 18 Oct 2026 14.31 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt 7.16pm, just around the time those Sunday night blues kick in, England’sChampions Cupcohort finally had something to cheer about. It was not pretty but after seven of their Prem rivals had failed to claim victory in the opening round of the competition, Saints survived a sizeable scare from Cardiff to put one on the board for the Prem, thanks in no small part to the excellent George Hendy.It might be harsh on some of the performances this weekend –Gloucester were immensein drawing with Bordeaux, Exeter mightily unlucky to be beaten in Toulouse – but zero wins would have been a crushing embarrassment for a league that has been feted for its attacking exploits so far this season. One out of eight is not a lot to shout about as it is.Ultimately first-half tries from youngsters James Pater and Toby Thame and second-half scores from Hendy and Fraser Dingwall were enough to see off Cardiff. Hendy also made the first try, stopped a certain Cardiff score and enhanced his reputation as a player who can make things happen for the Prem champions. “That has always been his forte, his super strength, George can break the game open, he can make breaks other people can’t,” said Northampton’s director of rugby, Phil Dowson.Credit to the visitors, however, who were less than impressed with the scheduling of this fixture given they run out again just five days later and felt forced to heavily rotate as a result. They scored two impressive tries and midway through the second half had Northampton fans fearing an upset.Quick GuideNorthampton 28-12 Cardiff: Teams and scorersShowNorthamptonPater (Smith 70); Sleightholme, Hutchinson, Thame (Dingwall 57), Hendy; Belleau, Mitchell (McParland 57); Fischetti (Els 62), Smith (Langdon 62), Kundiona (Neculai 53), Lockett, Van der Mescht (Prowse 53), Kemeny, Taylor (Ulcoq 67), ChickTriesPater, Thame, Hendy, DingwallConsBelleau 3, PaterSin-binBelleau (61)CardiffYoung; Grady, Millard (Adams 57), Emanuel, Bowen; Evans(Sheedy 62), Mulder (Davies 77); Southworth (Barratt 56), Hughes (capt), Wainwright(Cowell 65), Manz, Thornton, Paea(De la Rua 61), Thomas, Faletau (Lloyd 57;McNally 71)TriesMillard, GradyConEvansRefereeJérémy Rozier (Fr)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Cardiff’s frustrations are understandable. The head coach, Corniel van Zyl, confirmed the club made representations to the tournament organisers EPCR in the hope of moving the fixture to earlier in the weekend but received short shrift. “Bonkers,” was the assessment of Cardiff’s plight by Dowson. Accordingly, Van Zyl rang the changes but there was a first appearance for Taulupe Faletau since March. Northampton opted to chop and change too with Tommy Freeman, Henry Pollock, Alex Coles and Emmanuel Iyogun left out of the matchday 23.Sideways rain will always be a leveller and the opening 10 minutes here left you longing for the sugar rush of last weekend’s 119-point try fest. The first moment of quality yielded the first try, however. Hendy swerved his way through the Cardiff defence and charged clear, feeding the supporting Alex Mitchell, whose floated inside pass found Pater. Saints’ second try came after Rory Hutchinson’s inventive diagonal kick forced a Northampton scrum five metres out. Mitchell fed Hutchinson, who shipped on to Thame and there was no stopping the Northampton inside centre.View image in fullscreenGeorge Hendy roars in delight after scoring a try for Northampton.Photograph: David Rogers/Getty ImagesA period of scrappiness ensued and Cardiff certainly had their moments. They thought they had scored after a clever strike play near halfway put Mason Grady through a gap with Tom Manz appearing to go over. The referee, Jérémy Rozier, at the suggestion of the TMO, disallowed the score, however, insisting the ball had been dislodged in the tackle.Quick GuideExeter and Leicester beaten in FranceShowExeterslipped to a 43-40 defeat against 14-manToulousedespite Zack Wimbush scoring a hat-trick. In a thrilling start Wimbush scored for Exeter only a minute into the match, with Henry Slade adding the extras. Ange Capuozzo soon struck for the hosts, but Romain Ntamack was unable to convert before, who then went ahead through a penalty try.A frenetic seven-minute period saw the visiting full-back Sam Harris sent to the sin-bin before Toulouse prop Rodrigue Neti was shown a red card for a high tackle and Exeter pounced as Wimbush went over again with Slade’s kick successful.Toulouse responded through Joshua Brennan’s converted effort and a Teddy Thomas try, but the latter was shown a yellow card which allowed Exeter to regain control as Jack Yeandle and Stephen Varney both crossed, with Slade only able to convert the latter, to lead 26-24 at the break.They extended their advantage soon after the restart when Will Butt grounded and Slade converted, but they continued to be tested by Toulouse, who squeezed ahead as Matias Remue and Ntamack both scored in quick succession, with the fly-half converting both. Wimbush completed his hat-trick and Slade’s conversion put Exeter in front again, but Ben Hammersley was then shown yellow and Toulouse struck through Remue’s try to edge ahead.Slade sent a penalty wide in the final moments as Toulouse snatched a narrow victory.Ollie Chessum made a try-scoring return from injury butLeicesterfell short in their opener atPau. Archie van der Flier gave the visitors a flicker of hope when his 54th-minute try put his side within touching distance but the hosts  pulled away for a 41-17 bonus-point win.Leicester went into the game on the back of two  wins in the Gallagher Prem and their confidence was evident when the returning Chessum powered over in his first appearance of the season.But tries from Rodrigo Marta and Jon Zabala gave Pau a half-time lead and when they stretched their advantage through Marta’s second early in the second half, it looked all over for the visitors.Van der Flier had other ideas when he powered over, Billy Searle’s kick taking them back within seven points, but a silly penalty and a subsequent try from Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang all but sealed it for the French side.Pau secured their bonus point in the dying stages when Searle’s attempted pass was intercepted and Fabien Brau-Boirie blazed home to confirm the win.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.After the break an interception from the covering Pater denied Cardiff a certain score on the right but to their credit the visitors kept hammering away and after a tap-and-go penalty, the outside-centre Harri Millard had the strength to force his way over the line. Jarrod Evans’s conversion brought Cardiff to within a score.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAnd when Northampton’s fly-half Anthony Belleau was sent to the sin-bin for infringing near his own line on the hour mark, Cardiff were within two points when Grady was worked into space on the right. Evans, under pressure from the charging Ollie Sleightholme, missed the conversion however.Saints swiftly made him pay and after Cardiff failed to clear their lines on the restart, Dingwall put Hendy through a gap and the Northampton wing juggled the ball towards the line before gathering just in time to score. For good measure Hendy then rubber-stamped his fine performance by chasing down Josh Adams on the left. The 31-year-old Wales winger has lost a yard of pace but it was a significant intervention from Hendy, effectively extinguishing Cardiff’s hopes of victory.Dingwall added a fourth for Northampton at the death rounding off a far more workmanlike victory than eight days earlier. “The joy of it is both, there’s a balance [of both types of games],” added Dowson. “The stats will say only Saints won but I don’t think the English sides are too far away.”Explore more on these topicsChampions CupNorthamptonCardiff RugbyRugby unionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Kartal denied biggest win of career after Chwalinska fightback in Wuhan Open final | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal was denied her first major title after a 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 defeat by Maja Chwalinska in the final of the Wuhan Open in China
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal was denied her first major title after a 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 defeat by Maja Chwalinska in the final of the Wuhan Open in China
Content: Sonay Kartal will move into the world’s top 50 despite defeat in China.Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/ReutersView image in fullscreenSonay Kartal will move into the world’s top 50 despite defeat in China.Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/ReutersTennisKartal denied biggest win of career after Chwalinska fightback in Wuhan Open finalFrench Open finalist wins 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 for her first titleKartal will become new British No 1 after record runPress Association and Agence France-PresseSun 18 Oct 2026 09.51 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 12.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSonay Kartal missed out on winning the biggest title of her career as her brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a final defeat by Maja Chwalinska.Kartal has enjoyed her best tournament only a fortnight after returning from six months out with a back injury, but her efforts appeared to catch up with her as she faded in a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 loss.Netball enters brave new world as New Zealand stun AustraliaRead moreInstead it was Chwalinska who lifted her first WTA 1000 trophy – the first of her career at any level on the WTA Tour – after fighting back from a set and a break down. The 25‑year‑old made a stunning breakthrough earlier this season when she reached the French Open final as a qualifier, and she will now move towards the top 10.At 170 in the world, Kartal wasthe lowest-ranked player to reach a finalat this level since the format was introduced in 2009 and only the second British woman after Johanna Konta. She fell short of matching Konta, who won the Miami Open in 2017, but Kartal’s reward will be a new ranking of 50, making her the British No 1 for the first time.“It was a very physical battle and I think I had my chances and I think that’s maybe where the rust of six months off comes in,” Kartal said. “But overall I’m very happy with my performance. Obviously not the result I wanted and it’s going to sting for a little while but I think for me the positives this week outweigh that result today. So I’m leaving here head high and in a good spot overall.”Kartal, whose only tour title came at a small event in Tunisia in 2024, continued the form she had shown throughout the tournament in the opening set, immediately breaking broke the relatively weak Chwalinska serve.The Pole possesses an unconventional game, relying more on the use of spins, slices and angles than pace, but two of Kartal’s greatest strengths are her patience and game intelligence, and she dealt with the challenge admirably. She put Chwalinska under constant pressure and broke serve twice more to clinch the opening set.Given her long break and the physical intensity of this run, it was perhaps not a surprise to see Kartal call the trainer at the end of the first set. She was given a pill, which she took after saving three break points in the opening game of the second set. Fatigue was starting to show and, after breaking serve to lead 2-0, Kartal was unable to battle through another long game.There was a delay after the second point of the fifth game when Chwalinska broke a shoelace chasing a wide ball but the Pole’s defensive skills were beginning to get the better of Kartal and the 16th seed made it one set all.Kartal tried to get back on the front foot at the start of the decider but she was constantly pushed back by high balls from her opponent and Chwalinska overcame late nerves to clinch victory.“[This title] tastes very sweet,” Chwalinska said. “I feel like I still don’t realise that I won. But it feels special, because after French Open, it was obviously amazing, but then I had some tough moments.“I feel like people also were very rough towards me. And it took a toll on me as well. I’m just a human. But I kept working really hard and I’m just very grateful that my work paid off.”Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter each scored twice in Chelsea’s 6-2 win as Tottenham conceded six for the second successive WSL game
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter each scored twice in Chelsea’s 6-2 win as Tottenham conceded six for the second successive WSL game
Content: Lauren James celebrates her second and Chelsea’s third at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLauren James celebrates her second and Chelsea’s third at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueJames and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL againSuzanne Wrackat Stamford BridgeSun 18 Oct 2026 09.13 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTwo goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.Chelsea 6-2 Tottenham: Women’s Super League – live reactionRead moreJames’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.View image in fullscreenLauren James squeezes in Chelsea’s opener from the tightest of angles.Photograph: John Walton/PAThe bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.Quick GuideWSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% recordShowManchester Cityheld off a spirited fightback fromBrightonto close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League.Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles.Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea.London City Lionessesmade it a full house for the top three, beatingEverton2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control.Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.Manchester Unitedare up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom sideCharlton3-1.Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark.Aston Villastunned falteringLiverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal.Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half asWest HamdefeatedCrystal Palace1-0.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFour minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.View image in fullscreenChelsea retake the lead in the second half thanks to Ellie Carpenter’s first goal.Photograph: John Walton/PA“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueChelsea WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolition | Boxing | The Guardian
description: The WBO heavyweight champion targets big paydays against Hrgovic, Kabayel and Itauma after second round stoppage
Author: Donald McRae
Headline: The WBO heavyweight champion targets big paydays against Hrgovic, Kabayel and Itauma after second round stoppage
Content: Daniel Dubois (left) dominated Fabio Wardley in two rounds to retain his WBO heavyweight title on Saturday night.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAView image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois (left) dominated Fabio Wardley in two rounds to retain his WBO heavyweight title on Saturday night.Photograph: Nick Potts/PABoxing‘My time, my era’: Dubois sends out warning to rivals with Wardley demolitionWBO heavyweight champion targets big paydays against Hrgovic, Kabayel and Itauma after second round winDonald McRaeSun 18 Oct 2026 09.53 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThirty minutes afterDaniel Dubois had dismantled Fabio Wardleyin less than two rounds on Saturday night, his promoter Frank Warren shook his head in slight awe as he described the intensity before the annihilation: “I went in the dressing room beforehand like I normally do and I couldn’t have a conversation with Daniel because he was so zoned in and focused. It showed when he got in the ring. He went out there on a seek-and-destroy mission.”Dubois resembled a much bigger and heavier version of a young Mike Tyson as, wearing black trunks and a black cape, he walked to the ring with intense purpose. There was not a flicker of emotion as he marched quickly towards Wardley for their WBO world title rematch.Daniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO titleRead moreIn the first fight, five months ago, Dubois was knocked down after just 16 seconds. He was dropped again in the third round, before he went to work behind his jolting jab and proceeded to beat up a valiant Wardley who refused to surrender until rescued by the referee in the 11th round.The clear consensus was thatWardley would be a reduced figurein the rematch and that his only real hope boiled down to the fact that he still hits like a mule and that Dubois is regarded as a slow starter. But the champion was ready. “I was more focused than I was in May, big-time,” Dubois said. “It was go-time from the minute I put my gear on. Maybe the warm-up was more extensive than usual but I was in the zone quicker. Everyone was saying Fabio was going to start fast so I was ready for him.”Had he expected such a brutally quick stoppage? “I can’t say I did,” Dubois said. “I was prepared for a war. I wasn’t going to be denied. I refused to lose.”Dubois insisted that no heavyweight in the world could have withstood the ferocious blows he rained down on Wardley. His certainty was understandable as he looked formidable – even if Wardley’s famed punch resistance has dissipated. “Fabio has got a great chin,” Dubois pointed out and it’s true that Wardley has never been dropped. Even in Saturday’s dark whirlwind he took a standing count after just 17 seconds when a monstrous right hand left him crumpled against the ropes. Wardley was also still on his feet, while hunched over in a corner, when his trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel.After his victory, Dubois proclaimed that “this is my time, my era.”Only three men currently have the movement and skill to hold off a rampaging Dubois. Oleksandr Usyk remains the best heavyweight in the world and he has alreadydefeated Dubois twice. But the unbeaten Ukrainian master will turn 40 in January and he wants just one more fight in America. As he had appeared keen on facing a washed-up Deontay Wilder, it is likely that Usyk is in the mood for an easy last dance.Tyson Fury, who should beat Anthony Joshua in December, could be tempted by the riches of another lucrative all-British showdown against Dubois. In his prime, Fury would have dazzled Dubois with his awkward mobility and slippery skills. But Fury is 38 and a waning force.Moses Itauma is the third boxer with the speed and dexterity to trouble Dubois – but the 21-year-old prodigy suffered a severe setback when, having won every round against Filip Hrgovic, he ran out of steam and wasoverwhelmed in the ninth. It was a sobering reminder that Itauma has much to learn about the harsh realities of boxing.“I just want to know who’s next Frank,” Dubois said cheerfully.Warren explained that Hrgovic, the IBF champion, has a mandatory defence against Frank Sánchez in Croatia. The WBC version of the world title belongs to Agit Kabayel, a decent heavyweight who is a huge ticket-seller in Germany.View image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois said of his next potential opponent: ‘I’ll fight whoever’s next in line … whoever pays the most cash.’Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty ImagesHrgovic, Kabayel, Fury and Itauma are all promoted by Warren, who said: “The good thing is that everyone wants to fight. They’re fighting men. There will be great fights and, this will be music to Daniel’s ears, great money.”Dubois laughed in delight before he was asked who he would like to fight most. “I’ve heard talk about Kabayel but I’ll fight whoever’s next in line … whoever pays the most cash.”Hrgovic had been ringside and he suggested he had struggled with illness when losing a bruising battle to Dubois in 2024. The confident Croat promised to “smash” his rival next time.“Did he really say that?” Dubois asked in amusement before turning to the unlikely prospect of fighting Usyk for a third time. “Definitely. I’d love that. We’re coming out on top this time. We’ve made our mistakes but I’m a different fighter now.”Warren confirmed that he could easily imagine Fury accepting the challenge of facing Dubois while Itauma’s name was mentioned next.Itauma is the most naturally gifted heavyweight in Britain but Warren reminded us of his age. He also stressed that a future clash between Dubois and a more experienced Itauma would be “a gun fight” to fill a stadium.Dubois smiled with the look of a man who knows he could dominate heavyweight boxing for years. When asked if he would like to fight Itauma one day, Dubois nodded intently. “I hope so because I need dance partners.”Explore more on these topicsBoxingfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Panthers pile pain on slumping Eagles; Cardinals shock Rams | NFL | The Guardian
description: Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, while the Eagles’ tough start to the season continued
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, while the Eagles’ tough start to the season continued
Content: Nick Sirianni contemplates another loss for the Eagles.Photograph: Ricky Fitchett/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenNick Sirianni contemplates another loss for the Eagles.Photograph: Ricky Fitchett/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockNFLNFL roundup: Panthers pile pain on slumping Eagles; Cardinals shock RamsInjury-riddled Philadelphia fall to defeatChicago hold off Atlanta comeback in QB’s returnCardinals beat Rams with final play of gameAgenciesSun 18 Oct 2026 16.57 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 19.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCarolina Panthers 25–14 Philadelphia EaglesBryce Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns to Tommy Tremble, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score to lead the Carolina Panthers (3-2) past the injury-riddled Philadelphia Eagles (2-4). The Panthers had little trouble in the second half picking apart the Eagles, who were missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley. Hurts is on injured reserve and will miss at least four gameswith a blood clot in his calf. Tanner McKee started for Philadelphia and finished 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown.Chicago Bears 31–23 Atlanta FalconsCaleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, D’Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and the Chicago Bears (4-2) beat the Atlanta Falcons (2-4). The Bears led 31-7 before holding off Atlanta’s comeback attempt in the final quarter. Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon, who returned from a calf injury, had three sacks and two forced fumbles. Gordon’s big day was capped by a sack of Michael Penix Jr and forced fumble with 2:54 remaining and the Bears protecting a 31-23 lead.Arizona Cardinals 18-16 Los Angeles RamsChad Ryland kicked his sixth field goal, a 43-yarder as time expired, and the Arizona Cardinals rallied for a stunning victory over the Los Angeles Rams. Punter Ethan Evans kicked the go-ahead extra point after Colby Parkinson caught a touchdown pass from Matthew Stafford with 47 seconds to play for the vaunted Rams, who struggled all day before mounting a desperate final scoring drive. But the Cardinals immediately moved 36 yards into field goal range on Jalen Brooks’ long reception and an unnecessary roughness penalty on Josh Wallace. Three snaps later, Ryland buried his final kick to seal a shocking upset for Arizona. Evans came through with his first career placekick after new Rams kicker Blake Grupe injured his knee making a tackle in the first quarter. Both teams are 2-4 on the season.Buffalo Bills 33–30 Las Vegas RaidersJosh Allen passed for 255 yards and two touchdowns, and the Buffalo Bills (5-1) held off the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Allen’s second TD pass moved him into a tie with Hall of Famer Jim Kelly for the most in Bills franchise history. He showed his improvisational brilliance on that throw, when he avoided a sack andshot-putted the ball to Keon Colemanfor a 12-yard TD. James Cook rushed for a three-yard touchdown with 4:43 left to put the Bills ahead for good, and Tyler Bass made it a two-score game with a late field goal.Los Angeles Chargers 6–22 Kansas City ChiefsKenneth Walker III rushed for 128 yards and two touchdowns and Patrick Mahomes passed for 272 yards to boost the host Kansas City Chiefs ⁠to victory. Kansas City improved to 5-0 to remain the lone unbeaten team in the AFC. The skidding Chargers (0-6) are ⁠off to the franchise’s ⁠worst start since ​the 2000 San Diego Chargers lost their first 11 games during a 1-15 season. Los Angeles coach Jim Harbaugh started five games at quarterback for that team.Baltimore Ravens 10–13 Cleveland BrownsDeshaun Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards to set up Andre Szmyt’s 37-yard field goal on the final snap, and the Cleveland Browns rallied past the Baltimore Ravens. Cleveland’s first-year coach, Todd Monken, picked up an improbable victory over the Ravens, for whom he spent the previous three seasons as offensive coordinator. Cleveland relied on their defense for long stretches and got just enough playmaking from Watson in the end. The Ravens had Tyler Huntley at quarterback for the second straight week because Lamar Jackson has an ankle injury. Baltimore scored on their first two possessions but did nothing from there. Both teams have 4-2 records.New York Jets 19–26 New England PatriotsDrake Maye tossed three touchdown passes and the New England Patriots extended their winning streak to three games. Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for ⁠235 yards. Romeo Doubs, ⁠DeMario Douglas and ​Hunter Henry had New England’s touchdown receptions, while Douglas caught seven passes for 86 yards. New York’s Geno Smith completed ⁠20 of 30 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown but was intercepted for the first time this season. The Jets (2-4) got four ⁠field goals from Jason Sanders and a game-high 11 tackles (six solo) from Jamien Sherwood. Sanders ​pulled the Jets within 26-19 by ‌kicking a 36-yard field ‌goal with 32 seconds to play, but New England (4-2) recovered the onside kick.Pittsburgh Steelers 26–19 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (OT)Aaron Rodgers threw touchdown passes in the fourth quarter and overtime and Chris Boswell made four field goals to lead ⁠the Pittsburgh Steelers to a comeback overtime win. The Steelers (4-2) erased a 16-3 ⁠fourth quarter deficit with ⁠16 unanswered points ​in the period. The Bucs (1-5) tied the game at 19 with three seconds left on a 53-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin. Rodgers led a 12-play, 70-yard drive, capped by a six-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard with 3:15 left in overtime. Jalon Daniels, who ​made his third consecutive start for the injured ‌Baker Mayfield, scrambled 10 ‌yards to Tampa Bay’s own 37 for a first down on fourth- and-nine on the ‌Bucs’ ensuing drive. Five plays later, Daniels was sacked on fourth down by Jalen Ramsey on a corner blitz to end the game.Houston Texans 34–31 Jacksonville JaguarsKa’imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired, CJ Stroud threw three touchdown passes and the Houston Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars on the slick grass of Wembley Stadium. Cam Little’s 60-yard field goal had tied the game at 31-31 with just under two minutes left after Travis Hunter intercepted Stroud’s pass in the end zone. Hunter also hauled in a seven-yard touchdown pass at the other end – becoming just the fifth player in the Super Bowl era, including the playoffs, to score a touchdown and intercept a pass in the same game. Marvin Harrison Jr made his debut for the 2-4 Texans as Houston earned back-to-back wins to gain ground on the AFC South-leading Jaguars (4-2).New Orleans Saints 34–27 New York GiantsTyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a score, and the New Orleans Saints (2-4) scored 34 consecutive points, holding on to defeat the New York Giants (3-2-1) and end their three game-losing streak. Isaiah Stalbird forced a fumble on a kick return late in the first half that flipped the momentum in favor of the Saints. Giants fans streamed to the exits after Jameis Winston threw his second interception of the afternoon early in the fourth quarter, and the stands were half-empty by the time JJ McCarthy led multiple scoring drives and fell just short of an improbable comeback.Tennessee Titans 26–20 Indianapolis ColtsJoey Slye connected on a tie-breaking 49-yard field goal with 2:03 left on Sunday as the visiting Tennessee Titans upset ⁠the Indianapolis Colts for their first win of the season. It was the third field goal of the game for Slye, ⁠who added a ⁠44-yarder with 43 seconds ​remaining after Tennessee (1-5) got a fourth-down stop. The comeback from a 13-point halftime deficit gave head coach Robert Saleh his first win ⁠with the team. Cam Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Titans. Tennessee notched six sacks, ​including two apiece by Jeffery Simmons and ‌Jermaine Johnson II. Daniel Jones ‌hit 22 of 42 passes for 269 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for ‌Indianapolis (2-4) while Jonathan Taylor ran for 94 yards on 21 carries.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Four people killed in ‘violent, fast-moving’ fire at Canadian military base | Canada | The Guardian
description: Prime minister Mark Carney describes blaze as ‘one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime’
Author: Leyland Cecco
Headline: Prime minister Mark Carney describes blaze as ‘one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime’
Content: 1:46Canadian soldiers killed in fast-moving grass fire at military base – videoCanadaFour people killed in ‘violent, fast-moving’ fire at Canadian military basePrime minister Mark Carney describes blaze as ‘one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime’Leyland Ceccoin Toronto, Guardian staff and agenciesSun 18 Oct 2026 19.53 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 22.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFour people have been killed and dozens more seriously injured after a “violent, fast-moving” fire tore through one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta, the country’s prime minister said on Sunday.Mark Carney called the incident “one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime”.Winds up to 96km/h (60mph) fed the blaze, which broke out at 4pm on Saturday during high-intensity combat training at the base. Alberta premier Danielle Smith said at a press conference on Sunday evening that 39 people were in hospital after the fire, with at least 19 of them in a critical condition.Maj Gen Wade Rutland, commander of the 1st Canadian Division, said that a grass fire ignited in a training area of the military base, which spread quickly.The cause of the fire was being investigated, he said.The military identified those killed as Sgt Morgan Wong of the Loyal Edmonton Regiment and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light infantry. All four were serving with the battalion, based in Edmonton.Rutland said military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was contained before winds suddenly shifted, sending flames racing toward the soldiers.“The fire was a kilometre away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 36 seconds,” he said at a news conference in Edmonton.“I’ve certainly never seen anything like it,” he added.The fire broke out during high-intensity combat training involving Charlie Company of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light infantry, sweeping into the area where the simulated attacks were taking place.About 84 soldiers were in the company, which was split between a grenade range and an area where soldiers practised attacks on simulated enemy positions.“The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces whom we have lost. And I have asked the flags on all federal buildings to be flown at half-mast to honour them,” Carney told the nation in an address from Ottawa. “We are praying for the wounded.”Carney said he had requested a “detailed account” from military officials on the ground about what had happened.View image in fullscreenEmergency crews and military personnel gather at the Wainwright Health Centre on Saturday.Photograph: John Ulan/The Canadian Press/APThe country’s defence minister, David McGuinty,described the event as a “terrible incident” as he travelled to the scene to meet senior officials and first responders.“I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory,” he said, adding that the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) were involved in the investigation.McGuinty did not provide details about what caused the incident and theCanadian armed forces said on Sunday that its“immediate priority” was notifying next of kin and helping those affected by the fire.The armed forces and federal, provincial and local authorities were coordinating the emergency response, they said.Canada’s top soldier, Gen Jennie Carignan, who serves as chief of the defence staff, called the incident “a profoundly difficult moment for the entire Canadian armed forces”.View image in fullscreenThe nearby community of Wainwright was providing hospital and firefighting support.Photograph: Jennifer Gauthier/ReutersThe nearby community of Wainwright provided hospital and firefighting support. Flares were spotted in the sky and military medical paratroopers dropped in on a local school football field.Health staff in ‌Edmonton said a “code orange,” or mass-casualty ​event, was declared to coordinate ​the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright.A doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, 180km (112 miles) north-west of Wainwright, told Canada’s national broadcaster thatWainwright’s healthcare facilities had been inundated.“This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton,” Dr Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at the Royal Alexandra hospital, told CBC News. “It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15- to 25-year disaster.”Officials asked people in Edmonton to avoid the emergency department at the University of Alberta hospital in order to prioritise victims from the military base. Air ambulances were dispatched from Saskatoon and Edmonton.View image in fullscreenCanada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, said the nation was ‘in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces whom we have lost’.Photograph: Patrick Doyle/The Canadian Press/APJust 14% of Albertans want independence from Canada. Can a conference in a Calgary ballroom change that?Read moreThe fire at the military base swept into the area where the simulated attacks were taking place, crossing established firebreaks before being contained with help from municipal firefighters.The Canadian military said there were no indications of terrorism.On Sunday, the Alberta premier described the fire as “heartbreaking” and said it had affected many military personnel.“On behalf of the government of Alberta, I extend my deepest condolences to the families who have lost loved ones and wish those who have been injured a full recovery. Our thoughts are also with the military personnel, families and colleagues facing uncertainty and grief during this incredibly difficult time,” Smith said.The premier said many of the injured would require “weeks and months” of specialised, intensive medical care. She is due to travel to meet senior officials in Edmonton.The Saskatchewan premier, Scott Moe, said his province was sending assistance to Alberta but did not specify what resources were being deployed.View image in fullscreenCFB Wainwright is one of Canada’s busiest military bases.Photograph: Daphne Lemelin/AFP/Getty ImagesCFB Wainwright is one of Canada’s busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training.“On behalf of the Nato military committee, we extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the tragedy at CFB Wainwright, and our wishes for a full recovery to all the injured,” Adm Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, the chair of the Nato military committee, posted on social media. “Those who fell there served our common security, and the military committee will honour their memory.”Canada’s Conservative leader, Pierre Poilievre, said he had spoken with Carney and the defence minister to offer support to those affected by the fire.“Pray for Wainwright, everyone,” Poilievre said in a social media post. He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.Explore more on these topicsCanadaAmericasMark CarneynewsShareReuse this content

title: Times’s investigation adds more intrigue to infamous OJ Simpson case | OJ Simpson | The Guardian
description: Report reveals that a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up murder
Author: José Olivares
Headline: Report reveals that a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up murder
Content: OJ Simpson reacts with lawyers after court clerk announces not guilty verdict in his murder trial on 3 October 1995.Photograph: ReutersView image in fullscreenOJ Simpson reacts with lawyers after court clerk announces not guilty verdict in his murder trial on 3 October 1995.Photograph: ReutersOJ SimpsonTimes’s investigation adds more intrigue to infamous OJ Simpson caseReport reveals that a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up murderJosé OlivaresSun 18 Oct 2026 19.35 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 19.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn in-depth investigation by theNew York Timesis raising further questions about the high-profile OJ Simpson case, in which the former football player was accused in the 1990s of killing his ex-wife – and whether a shady mobster-turned-informant may have been involved in helping cover up the murder.The Times’s investigation revealed thatCaliforniaprosecutors were unable to fully investigate whether Simpson, who was accused but not convicted of his ex-wife’s murder, may have had an accomplice at the scene of the crime.The extensive journalistic investigation, based on previously sealed court records and interviews, adds further intrigue to the infamous Simpson case. No one was ever criminally convicted for the 1994 murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.That year, Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman were found stabbed to death outside her home inLos Angeles. The American professional football player and actor, OJ Simpson, was suspected in the murder. Simpson’s prosecution gained international attention and became a media spectacle, being deemed the “trial of the century”.Simpson was acquitted by a jury in 1995 after a lengthy trial. The Los Angeles police department, which investigated the case, had a long history of racism. Simpson’s attorneys pointed to the racist policing practices and the department’s handling of key evidence, helping them secure the acquittal. Simpson was later held liable for the deaths by a jury in a civil case.But the New York Times has now revealed that a shady informant began revealing information about Simpson’s case towards the end of the prosecution. The informant, a wealthy mobster named Joseph Ippolito, had become a snitch after spending years on the run from the federal government.The information Ippolito had may have been key to the trial, but it was far too late for the prosecution to include his testimony.Ippolito, a longtime drug runner throughout the US known as Joey, came from the New Jersey underworld, where his father was a player within the DeCavalcante crime family, a major Italian American criminal organization. After a stint in prison for trafficking drugs in the east coast, he moved to California in the late 1980s and managed an Italian restaurant.There, he was able to embed himself in the inner circles of the Los Angeles elite. Ippolito befriended Al Cowlings, a former football star and close friend ofOJ Simpson. But while he spent time with Los Angeles celebrities, Ippolito continued selling and trafficking drugs.In 1992, he was arrested by authorities again in a sting operation. But in May 1994, eight months after his sentencing, Ippolito escaped from his Florida prison. His brother helped him arrive back in Los Angeles, where he remained in hiding as a wanted fugitive.That year, the murder of Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman took place in Los Angeles. When authorities attempted to arrest OJ Simpson, he fled. His friend Cowlings, the former football player, led the police on a widely-publicized chase through Los Angeles with Simpson in the car.After Simpson’s arrest, officials found Ippolito’s information in Cowlings’ wallet, leading them to urgently search for the mobster-at-large. Eventually they found Ippolito and arrested him. But he decided to flip and become an informant for the US government.As an informant, Ippolito revealed information about various drug deals throughout the country and helped federal agencies set up sting operations. But Ippolito also reportedly shared information with the government about the Los Angeles murders.The New York Times raises three separate theories for Ippolito’s involvement in the Simpson case, which he was seemingly willing to share with authorities:1) In one version, Ippolito told federal prosecutors he had information he learned from Cowlings about the murders, including the supposed location of the missing weapon.2) In another version, Ippolito’s brother told a reporter with the Times that Ippolito may have been at the scene of the killings. The brother said Ippolito literally had blood on his hands.3) And in a third version, Ippolito was prepared to help Simpson escape during the wild police chase throughout Los Angeles.“Taken together, the material points in different directions but veers significantly from the official account that has been proffered by the police and prosecutors,” the New York Times reports. “With many of the key players now dead, it’s possible the full truth will never be known.”Ippolito’s brother, who told the Times he had seen his brother’s hands with blood on them, later asked the publication for money and then recanted his statement to the publication. According to the report, the brother said he had been “offered a ton of money” to share his story elsewhere, likely a television program.The extent of Ippolito’s involvement is not fully known. Authorities interviewed by the Times expressed doubts on how involved Ippolito was and the value of his information in the case.Explore more on these topicsOJ SimpsonCaliforniaUS crimeWest CoastLos AngelesnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘We are beyond heartbroken’: Cindy Crawford, Rande and Kaia Gerber share tributes to Presley | Celebrity | The Guardian
description: Family post emotional statements to Instagram a month after their son and brother died at a rehab facility
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Family post emotional statements to Instagram a month after their son and brother died at a rehab facility
Content: Rande Gerber and Cindy Crawford with their son Presley Gerber, who died on 20 September.Photograph: Rodin Eckenroth/WireImageView image in fullscreenRande Gerber and Cindy Crawford with their son Presley Gerber, who died on 20 September.Photograph: Rodin Eckenroth/WireImageCelebrity‘We are beyond heartbroken’: Cindy Crawford, Rande and Kaia Gerber share tributes to PresleyFamily post emotional statements to Instagram a month after their son and brother died at a rehab facilityPress AssociationSun 18 Oct 2026 18.52 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 20.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCindy Crawford and Rande Gerber have said they are “beyond heartbroken” in a tribute to their “sweet beautiful” son, Presley.Their eldest childdied aged 27at a rehab facility on 20 September, according to Los Angeles county medical examiner records. The cause of his death has not been disclosed.Crawford and Gerber posted an emotional statement on Instagram on Sunday.“We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother,” it said. “We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years.“He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.Death of 27-year-old Presley Gerber being investigated as suspected overdoseRead more“We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain.“Til we meet again our sweet boy.”The message was signed “with love forever” from Crawford and Gerber and their daughter, Kaia Gerber.Kaia, who like her mother is a model, also expressed her support in the comments, shared a message on her own page alongside a carousel of images and videos of herself with Presley.In a letter addressed to her brother, she wrote: “Prez, I don’t have the words. Maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along.”She wrote that she had “none of the answers” and could not articulate the “magnitude” of losing her brother.“You know how much I loved being your sister. It has always been, and will forever be, my favourite thing about myself.”The letter described her older brother as “inherently good” and her “ultimate teacher”, recounting childhood memories as she reflected on her grief.“I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you,” Kaia she. “How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can’t reach for you in. I don’t know how to do that yet.”She concluded: “My best buddy, my great protector, the hardest I’ve ever laughed and the one true love of my life. You lit all of my candles and took all of my monsters away, and I love you.”The post was set to the song First I Was by Jake Minch, which Kaia described as “the last thing we talked about”.The actors Taylor Lautner and Patrick Schwarzenegger, the singer Suki Waterhouse and the socialite Paris Hilton commented on the post.“My heart breaks for you and your family,” Hilton wrote. “Presley was truly one of a kind, and I feel so lucky to have known him. I’ll always remember him with so much love.”Presley was signed by IMGModelswhen he was 15 and modelled for brands including Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana and Bottega Veneta.He spoke frequently about his struggles with depression and substance abuse.Explore more on these topicsCelebrityBereavementSocial mediaModelsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Zack Polanski says application of Zionism is racist and no state has right to exist | Green party | The Guardian
description: Green leader in England and Wales calls ‘debates about words’ unhelpful and denies recent motion was controversial
Author: Kiran Stacey
Headline: Green leader in England and Wales calls ‘debates about words’ unhelpful and denies recent motion was controversial
Content: The Green Party leader in England and Wales, Zack Polanski, spoke to the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday.Photograph: Jeff Overs/PAView image in fullscreenThe Green Party leader in England and Wales, Zack Polanski, spoke to the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday.Photograph: Jeff Overs/PAGreen partyZack Polanski says application of Zionism is racist and no state has right to existGreen leader in England and Wales calls ‘debates about words’ unhelpful and denies recent motion was controversialKiran StaceyPolicy editorSun 18 Oct 2026 13.38 EDTFirst published on Sun 18 Oct 2026 06.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleZack Polanski has said Zionism in its current form is racist, that no country has a right to exist, and that theGreen party motionon the issue was not controversial.The leader of theGreen partyin England and Wales gave an unapologetic interview to the BBC on Sunday two weeks after his party approved a motion equating Zionism with racism.Polanski did not attend the vote, prompting accusations of a lack of leadership, but he made clear he agreed with the broad thrust of it even if he felt it was unhelpful to have what he called a “debate about semantics”.Asked by the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg whether he thought Zionism was racist, Polanski said: “I don’t think this is actually controversial.“What’s controversial is that 75,000 Palestinians have been murdered in the last few years, including more child amputees than ever in modern history. So when you take that to account, the fact that they’re being murdered because they’re Palestinian – that’s very obviously a racist ideology.”He added: “I think Zionism is racism in the practical application of it. Now the conference had a debate about the motion, about the word. I said I think debates about words are unhelpful, and I still think that.”Asked whether he believedIsraelhad a right to exist, Polanski, who is Jewish, said: “I don’t think any state has a right to exist under international law,” adding that the idea of a two-state solution was “for the birds” given Israel’s opposition to it.He also insisted he had no regrets about the way he had handled the recent controversy, despite criticism from some prominent Jewish Green members,including Vivien Lichtenstein, the chair of the Jewish Greens.Polanski said: “I’m not sorry at all. Vivien is someone I’ve had respect for and do have respect for, and partly co-founded the Jewish Greens together … Actually, when the Jewish Greens were surveyed about this motion, a majority supported it.”In response,Lichtenstein later said: “Zack should have joined conference online, listened to the speeches for and against and, crucially, spoken for those amendments he supported, then voted.“None of that took an inordinate amount of time. There was no excuse for his not participating.”She also said polling of Jewish greens on the Zionism motion showed they were evenly split, contrary to Polanski’s claims.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLabour councils told to end agreements with Greens who do not condemn ‘Zionism is racism’ policyRead morePolanski’s defiant interview comes after the most difficult two weeks of his leadership of the party since he took over last September, during which he has endured the fallout from the conference vote andlost the Holborn and St Pancras byelection.His strategy of shifting his party to the left, focusing on economically populist ideas and leaning into debates onPalestineand Gaza initially paid dividends, with the party jumping from about 10% in the polls to 18% earlier this year.In recent months, however, the party has tumbled, beset byquestions over his tax affairs, apublic spat with the policeafter the Golders Green attack and the recent row over Zionism.He said on Sunday that he was confident voters would return to his party once they had seen more of Andy Burnham’s leadership of the country. “People more and more will see from Andy Burnham a change in rhetoric, but not a change in action, and know the Green party have been right all along,” he said.Explore more on these topicsGreen partyZack PolanskiIsraelPalestineAntisemitismGazanewsShareReuse this content

title: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III | William Shakespeare | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysis
Author: Dalya Alberge
Headline: Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysis
Content: A Royal Shakespeare Company production of Edward III. It has been long thought Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes.Photograph: Geraint Lewis/ArenaPALView image in fullscreenA Royal Shakespeare Company production of Edward III. It has been long thought Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes.Photograph: Geraint Lewis/ArenaPALWilliam ShakespeareScholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward IIIExclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysisDalya AlbergeSun 18 Oct 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDramatic new evidence concludes that the play Edward III should be added to William Shakespeare’s canon, and also that it was a major collaboration with his contemporary rivalChristopher Marlowe.The history was published anonymously in 1596, and it has long been thought that Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer.He said: “That’s the new finding, that both Shakespeare, now confirmed beyond doubt, and Marlowe, unexpectedly found for the first time, are present in the play, and therefore it represents a newly found collaboration between the two.“It has massive implications for our understanding of the relationship between the two most important dramatists of this period. This changes both the Shakespeare canon and the Marlowe canon and will be of significant international interest.”View image in fullscreenA portrait of William Shakespeare from the title page of the 1623 first folio.Illustration: GraphicaArtis/Getty ImagesLoughnane, a reader in early modern studies at the University of Kent and general editor of the Oxford Marlowe editorial project, collaborated on the study with Brett Greatley-Hirsch, a professor of renaissance literature and textual studies at the University of Leeds.Edward III did not appear in the 1623 first folio collection of Shakespeare’s plays. Loughnane edited it for the 2016 New Oxford Shakespeare: Complete Works, acknowledging that a couple of scenes had probably been written by him, and the play had also appeared in a 2005 volume. Loughnane also co-authored the Canon and Chronology study in the New Oxford Shakespeare: Authorship Companion, which made the case for Shakespeare’s part-authorship, but acknowledged a need for further research.Loughnane said: “Our new research suggests that Marlowe is Shakespeare’s collaborator on Edward III. This is the first time this case has been made seriously.”The researchers used various forms of computerised linguistic analysis in comparing Edward III with securely attributed works by 10 dramatists active between the late 1580s and the mid-1590s. In one test, 23 segments – “the lion’s share” – were identified as being written by Shakespeare, while nine segments were classified as Marlowe, whose works include Doctor Faustus.Loughnane said these findings were particularly significant because a 2016 study had found that Marlowe was a co-author of Shakespeare’s threeHenry VIplays: “Their collaboration on Edward III in 1592 suggests a more sustained writing relationship in their mid-to-late 20s.”Marlowe died aged just 29, after a brawl in a lodging house in 1593. “We have become accustomed to thinking of Marlowe and Shakespeare as rivals – two outstanding authors, born within a few weeks of one another, making their names in the same theatrical world of the late 1580s and early 1590s,” Loughnane said. “But we now know that their relationship was much more complicated than that. They were not simply rivals or influences on one another.”View image in fullscreenA portrait thought to be of Christopher Marlowe.Photograph: Pictures from History/Universal Images Group/Getty ImagesRather than attributing particular lines to either author, the study focused on linguistic features and the distribution of certain “marker” words, such as “martial”, which are typically present in Marlowe’s plays and correspondingly atypical in the plays of other dramatists. They also suggest Shakespeare’s authorship of segments, “which may overlap with bits of writing he did not do”, and Marlowe’s authorship of other segments.The analysis confirms that a speech from the beginning of scene 13 was written by Shakespeare, when a sudden and ominous darkening of the sky causes fear in the French camp, and King Jean says: “A sudden darkness hath defaced the sky …”The analysis concludes that a speech from the final scene of the play was written by Marlowe: “Great servitor to bloody Mars in arms, / The Frenchman’s terror and his country’s fame.”Greatley-Hirsch said: “What makes the evidence particularly compelling is that we’re not relying on a single verbal parallel or statistical test. Different forms of analysis, looking at different features of the language, appear to repeatedly distinguish Marlowe’s writing from Shakespeare’s within the play.”The research will be published in the Shakespeare Quarterly later this year. Insights into Shakespeare’s early career are also explored in Loughnane’s forthcoming book, Shakespeare at Thirty, to be published by Princeton University Press this week.Loughnane has also curated an exhibition about the life and times of Marlowe in the playwright’s native Canterbury.The Making of Marloweruns until 22 November at the Beaney House of Art & Knowledge.Explore more on these topicsWilliam ShakespeareChristopher MarlowenewsShareReuse this content

title: The next ayahuasca? Gabon fights to protect sacred plant from US drug companies | Plants | The Guardian
description: Iboga root, central to several Gabonese ritual traditions, is believed to have huge potential for use in treating addiction and some mental illnesses
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Iboga root, central to several Gabonese ritual traditions, is believed to have huge potential for use in treating addiction and some mental illnesses
Content: A Bwiti ceremony where participants consume the bitter iboga root bark.Photograph: Jorge Fernández/LightRocket/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA Bwiti ceremony where participants consume the bitter iboga root bark.Photograph: Jorge Fernández/LightRocket/Getty ImagesThe age of extinctionPlantsThe next ayahuasca?
