Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something differentSun 18 Oct 2026 15.56 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 18.32 EDTShareAt the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot ofManchester Unitedchief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun.Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.‘Like a fresh start’: Michael Carrick relieved by Manchester United’s draw at LeedsRead moreHow do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For nowa hard-fought pointis perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.This was a dual-track football match between Leeds and Manchester United, on the face of it a good, even game between two teams of well-matched players.A 1-1 drawwas fair in the end, although Leeds played well and probably should have won. But of course they won’t be the story.Instead this game had already been billed as that familiar thing, a referendum on the future ofMichael Carrick. A stay of execution for a week or two. Or another livestreamed firing squad for the Super Sunday cameras.There has been a predictable sense of low comedy about Carrick’s own transformation in the United dugout this season. It was always going to be the case that his widely praised qualities in victory, blazer, T-shirt, jawline, inscrutable sense of calm, would become his fatal flaws in defeat.Where’s the passion, the whirling arms, the range of tailored collars? At Elland Road Carrick simply looked drained in the second half as United were pegged back and overrun at times, the beard a little more ragged, the hair unkempt but still sweeping, the look of a brave, doomed tugboat captain resigned now to the approaching tsunami wave on the horizon.A point leaves United 13th in the league and still struggling to reverse a dreadful start to the season. But it was a good game for two people. First for Carrick, who remains a million miles away from creating the problems afflicting this club, even if you accept that his presence as head coach is one of them.Michael Carrick did not hire Michael Carrick. Getting rid of Michael Carrick is, by definition, not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. But it might just help to prolong them. Whatever his ultimate ceiling, it is surely worth keeping him just to try, for once, to do something different.View image in fullscreenThe Manchester United director of football, Jason Wilcox (centre), and chief executive officer Omar Berrada (right) watch on at Elland Road.Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PAThis was also a good game for Lisandro Martínez, who went off injured at half-time with United 1-0 up, and who was also vindicated in his allegedly controversial (translation: entirely correct)comments on the club hierarchyin midweek.United’s energetic first-half performance clarified one half of this. The players are committed in support of the manager, at least to the best of their ability. The second half made the other half of the argument, that this remains a mismatched, lopsided, cut-and-paste squad, always likely to be pulled apart by opponents as urgent as this Leeds team, which fully deserves its current seventh place in the table.The problems are so obvious it is barely worth repeating them. But here goes. The third-richest club in the world played a second half with three of its back four out of position. Harry Maguire, signed under Ole Gunnar Solskjær, remains the best straight defender. But Maguire is also essentially a man-shaped solid wood armoire in a pair of shorts at this stage in his career, always the slowest person on any pitch, which means you will not be able to cover space, play a high line or counterattack without leaving yourself exposed to the counter-counter.So good luck, guys. And remember Omar, who gave you this whisky bottle and loaded pistol of a squad, will be watching.This was made painfully clear after half-time as Martínez went off and Noussair Mazraoui came on. Leeds scored an equaliser that felt structurally inevitable. They found space down their right side repeatedly. At times they seemed to be constantly peppering the seats behind the United goal, like a group of kids hammering a ball against a garage door. By the end Leeds had more possession, more shots on target and just looked a happier, better structured entity than the travelling heritage exhibit at the other end.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe key point here is to accept that all of this is entirely logical. This is not a mystery, a haunted house, a place of bad voodoo. Why do we talk about Manchester United so much? For obvious reasons. It’s a massive part of the English football landscape. Mainly, though, because this is a story of mind-bending waste, real-time elite-level incompetence played out on a weekly basis.Yes, you could sack Michael Carrick. It won’t change much. Let’s destroy Eddie Howe for a bit instead. But the available evidence suggests every single person making executive decisions here is outmatched and outmanoeuvred.There is a reason Manchester United feels like one of those high street legacy chain shops just before it collapses, piles of Quality Street by the door, a rat in the lingerie department, destined to become a pop-up vape shop run by Albanian money launderers. There’s a reason it feels so badly run. This is because: it is.View image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez, who criticised the Manchester United hierarchy in midweek, went off injured at half-time against Leeds.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersWe know the Glazer ownership has zero interest in minding the details, that this has been a wonderful acquisition whatever the performance on the pitch, an asset supremely sweated. We know also that Sir Jim Ratcliffe is pub-level incoherent on the details he promised to fix. Remember when he was going to sit down and decide what the “style of football” would be? How’s that working out?Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on CarrickRead moreInstead Carrick is left shuffling a first XI acquired by endlessly revolving administrations. Here United had four defenders signed under Erik ten Hag, two Ruben Amorim recruits, two from the mist-shrouded age of Solskjær. No players were recruited under Ralf Rangnick, of course. But then Rangnick wanted to sign Erling Haaland, Luis Díaz, and Julian Álvarez, which all sounds far too sensible.An organisation can be built with many hands. But not when so many of those hands appear to be so far from best in class it’s hard to work out which class they’re supposed to be attending. John Murtough, the former Manchester United football director, is currently director of global development at Atalanta, who have a 24,000-seat stadium and almost zero global presence. Meanwhile Berrada, the axeman, seems entirely invulnerable from the axe himself, despite the fact his job seems to orbit around resolving the consequences of his own mistakes.United probably will sack their current manager before the year is out. This is the way this machine has to operate, always looking to buy itself, and those in the executive seats, a little more time on the payroll, an entity that has been hollowed out and allowed to rust, run on buzzwords and brown paper and string. Meanwhile, over to you Michael. We’ll see you next week, and maybe even the week after that, for more of exactly the same.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedLeeds UnitedMichael CarrickanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Air Force officer killed in rappelling accident before UTSA’s game against Navy | College football | The Guardian
description: An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game
Content: The incident happened before UTSA’s game on Saturday.Photograph: John Rivera/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe incident happened before UTSA’s game on Saturday.Photograph: John Rivera/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesCollege footballAir Force officer killed in rappelling accident before UTSA’s game against NavyOfficer fell from rafters during pregame displayMan treated on field before being taken to hospitalGuardian sportSun 18 Oct 2026 10.03 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 10.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game against Navy on Saturday.The officer, who has not been named, was taking part in an event to celebrate UTSA’s Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans night. He fell on to the field while rappelling down from the stadium rafters. He was treated on the field before being taken away on a stretcher. He later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Nellis Air Force Base said he was part of the 6th Combat Training Squadron. The unit helps train military members to rappel down from helicopters.In video of the incident, the crowd could be heard reacting when the officer fell to the field. The Alamodome roof is around 170ft above the field.“There was something – you could just tell that the energy was just gone [from the crowd],” UTSA coach Jeff Traylor said after the game. “I’ve never had to deal with anything like that before. It just puts things in perspective. It really does.”The start of the game was delayed for around 10 minutes after the incident.“We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s game,” UTSA said in a statement. “Our heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with the soldier who was affected, his family and his military colleagues.”Explore more on these topicsCollege footballSan AntonioCollege sportsTexasUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Noni Madueke scored the only goal of the game as Arsenal left it late to snatch a 1-0 victory against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Noni Madueke scored the only goal of the game as Arsenal left it late to snatch a 1-0 victory against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground
Content: Noni Madueke celebrates the winning goal for Arsenal.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenNoni Madueke celebrates the winning goal for Arsenal.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianPremier LeagueMadueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victoryDavid Hytnerat the City GroundSun 18 Oct 2026 13.39 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season. Arsenal, meanwhile,had drawn 0-0on their previous two visits to this part of the east Midlands. They had only one win in five here.Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on CarrickRead moreIt was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions.Arsenaldid not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot on target. How Noni Madueke made it count.On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.View image in fullscreenLiam Delap holds off Ezri Konsa at the City Ground.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianForest refused to accept the inevitable. Chris Wood, on as a substitute, delayed too long and saw Rice block. Murillo, of all players, danced inside from the left and curled off target. Delap was denied at the death by a thunderous Ezri Konsa block tackle. But it did feel inevitable. Forest, who missed the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, might have played all night and not scored. Arsenal had not forgotten their previous away fixture –the 3-0 defeat at Brighton. It remains the only blot on their season.Arsenal had kicked off six points behind Manchester City, who have been perfect on the field in the league this season. Will it matter when the sanctions for their rule breaches are meted out? All Arsenal can do is play the situation as it stands and this was an occasion when the result was everything.Mikel Arteta’s team dominated the ball. As they were always likely to do. They were determined to be patient. And yet they were flat and predictable until the closing stages. The lack of incisive movement was glaring. That said, Forest were compact out of possession in a 5-4-1 formation and hard to break down. They were resolved not to give up any easy yards.Arsenal played their patterns. They tried to suck the life out of the home crowd, working on the principle that it is difficult for fans to get animated if their team do not have the ball. The first half drifted by in a lazy Sunday afternoon haze, no shots on target for either side.Delap carried the physical fight; the Forest centre-forward was a willing and direct runner and he won a free-kick off Rice just outside the Arsenal box on 44 minutes. Neco Williams thumped it at Bruno Guimarães, who went down and stayed down. The Forest support were unhappy at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. “Are you City in disguise?” they chanted.View image in fullscreenNoni Madueke fires home – via a deflection – the only goal of the game.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianCould a set piece provide the breakthrough? It felt the likeliest route. Murillo headed wide from a Forest corner in the 20th minute and was bloodied into the bargain; there was a whistle for a foul in the mass of bodies inside the six-yard box. At the other end, Kai Havertz headed over from a Rice free-kick on 37 minutes. He had a good look at the ball and was well-placed. It was a decent chance.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionArsenal have been a little barren in the first half this season. This was the seventh time in 10 matches since the Community Shield that they had failed to score in one. It has not been a problem. They needed to raise their levels for the second half.Arteta’s first change was Madueke for Eberechi Eze on the left wing; an admission that the latter had failed to exert an influence. There was also a triple substitution on 66 minutes, the manager sending on Jurriën Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyökeres for Ben White, Guimarães and Havertz. He needed to shake things up because nothing was happening for his team. It was Forest who pushed after the restart, with Delap continuing to put himself about. He asked questions of Gabriel Magalhães, albeit the Arsenal defender tended to have the answers.The minutes ticked down, the contest narrowing to a fine point and we waited to see whether there could be a moment, one big chance. Martin Ødegaard almost provided it in the 72nd minute when he released Timber with a lovely pass up the inside right. When he pulled back, Rice lifted wastefully high.Glasner’s decision to introduce Ibrahim Sangaré for Dan Ndoye shortly afterwards was telling. Sangaré’s mission was to bolster the Forest midfield and yet he was slow to react to a half-cleared ball. When Rice played the pass, Madueke took over.“We showed a champion spirit,” Madueke said. “Maybe last season, this game might not have gone for us. We have the extra belief and mentality.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueNottingham ForestArsenalmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Auburn stun No 1 Georgia on last-gasp field goal as top-ranked teams fall in successive weeks | College football | The Guardian
description: Alex McPherson’s field goal as time expired lifted Auburn to a 27-24 upset of Georgia, extending a historic run of defeats for college football’s No 1 teams
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Alex McPherson’s field goal as time expired lifted Auburn to a 27-24 upset of Georgia, extending a historic run of defeats for college football’s No 1 teams
Content: Auburn’s Keshaun Singleton catches a first-quarter touchdown pass against Georgia during the Tigers’ stunning 27-24 upset of the top-ranked Bulldogs on Saturday in Athens.Photograph: Todd Kirkland/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAuburn’s Keshaun Singleton catches a first-quarter touchdown pass against Georgia during the Tigers’ stunning 27-24 upset of the top-ranked Bulldogs on Saturday in Athens.Photograph: Todd Kirkland/Getty ImagesCollege footballAuburn stun No 1 Georgia on last-gasp field goal as top-ranked teams fall in successive weeksAlex McPherson’s 34-yard kick seals 27-24 upsetGeorgia lose two interceptions and late fumbleAgenciesSat 17 Oct 2026 21.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlex McPherson kicked a game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired and Auburn, led by quarterback Byrum Brown’s dominant running game, upset No 1 Georgia 27-24 on Saturday.It was the second straight week the top team in the AP Top 25 lost to an unranked opponent after then-No 1 Texas fell to Oklahoma last Saturday. Auburn’s win meant the team ranked No 1 in the AP Top 25 lost in consecutive weeks for the first time since October 1990, according to Sportradar.Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton led a long game-tying touchdown drive in the fourth quarter but lost a fumble with 58 seconds remaining and the Bulldogs driving for a potential go-ahead field goal.Stockton, who also threw two interceptions, fumbled on a run from the Auburn 46-yard line. Safety Sylvester Smith-Reed recovered for the Tigers at the Auburn 44. A roughing-the-passer penalty on Georgia’s Gabe Harris Jr helped set up McPherson’s game-winning kick. Auburn players swarmed the field.“It’s pretty neat,” said Auburn’s first-year coach, Alex Golesh. “I’m really proud of our guys. Really proud of them.“We’re going to build Auburn back to where everybody wants it, one game at a time. Just hang with us.”Brown ran for 115 yards and a touchdown on 26 carries and added a touchdown pass.View image in fullscreenAuburn kicker Alex McPherson celebrates his game-winning field goal on Saturday.Photograph: Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesGeorgia (6-1, 4-1 Southeastern Conference) saw their streaks of nine straight wins over Auburn and 53 consecutive wins over unranked teams come to an end in a loss that will also end the Bulldogs’ brief one-week stay atop the AP top 25.Auburn (4-2, 2-2) beat the Bulldogs on the ground, outrushing Georgia 192-113. Running back Nate Frazier returned from a rib injury to start for Georgia but was ineffective, gaining only 19 yards on nine carries.Georgia trailed 24-14 before rallying with a 42-yard field goal by Peyton Woodring. Stockton led a game-tying touchdown drive that began at the Georgia six-yard line and covered 94 yards in 13 plays, capped by his four-yard pass to London Humphreys.Stockton’s two interceptions doubled his previous season total through six games. The Bulldogs were also hurt by mistakes, including three personal foul penalties.“We helped them,” said Georgia coach Kirby Smart. “We had three turnovers and critical penalties. ... We had some really, really untimely, uncharacteristic and undisciplined penalties.”After Georgia took a 14-0 lead, Auburn scored the next 24 points.Georgia looked dominant in the opening minutes, even after Stockton had to leave after hitting the field helmet-first on the opening play. Ryan Puglisi completed all three of his passes, including a 41-yarder to Craig Dandridge Jr, before Dwight Phillips’ 15-yard touchdown run.Stockton returned for the next possession and threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to tight end Lawson Luckie for a 14-0 lead.Auburn responded with a physical, run-first attack led by the 235lb Brown, who was effective both on designed runs and when taking off after dropping back to pass.Top-ranked teams had won 93 consecutive home games against unranked opponents since LSU lost to Arkansas 50-48 in double overtime on 23 November 2007.Explore more on these topicsCollege footballCollege sportsUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace  | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Brighton scored three times in the first 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez from 51 metres, and then piled on more misery as they beat Crystal Palace 5-0
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Brighton scored three times in the first 10 minutes, including Diego Gómez from 51 metres, and then piled on more misery as they beat Crystal Palace 5-0
Content: Crystal Palace's Walter Benítez sticks out a flailing arm in vain as Diego Gómez’s audacious halfway-line shot puts Brighton 2-0 up.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCrystal Palace's Walter Benítez sticks out a flailing arm in vain as Diego Gómez’s audacious halfway-line shot puts Brighton 2-0 up.Photograph: Rob Newell/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueGómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal PalaceEd Aaronsat the Amex StadiumSun 18 Oct 2026 11.06 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.Leeds United 1-1 Manchester United: Premier League – live reactionRead moreThe concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February afterPalace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.View image in fullscreenYasin Ayari’s deflected effort results in Brighton’s third goal.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez.The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThings got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood scoring from close range six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBrighton & Hove AlbionCrystal Palacematch reportsShareReuse this content

title: European football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1 | European club football | The Guardian
description: Lyon lead Ligue 1 on goal difference over four other clubs after holding on to beat Nice with 10 men
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lyon lead Ligue 1 on goal difference over four other clubs after holding on to beat Nice with 10 men
Content: Lyon players embrace after Tanner Tessmann scored their winner.Photograph: Pauline Figuet/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLyon players embrace after Tanner Tessmann scored their winner.Photograph: Pauline Figuet/Getty ImagesEuropean club footballEuropean football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1Five teams level on points after Monaco lose to LorientReal Madrid ease past Sevilla with Mbappé doubleAgenciesSun 18 Oct 2026 14.36 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 18.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTen-manLyonheld on for a 2-1 comeback victory overNiceto move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pacesetters Monaco lost for the first time this season. Five teams are level on 14 points at the top of the table with Lyon heading Paris Saint-Germain,Paris FC, Lille and Monaco on goal difference.It was a close run affair forLyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura’s dismissal 20 minutes from time.Côte d’Ivoire forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring forNiceon 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied a stoppage-time equaliser by a tight offside call.Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.Noah Cadiou’s second-half penalty forLorientpreventedMonacoreturning to the top of Ligue 1 as they fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.Finnish goalkeeper Lukas Hradecky dived the right way, but Cadiou placed his spot-kick into the corner, to handMonacotheir first league defeat of the season.Monaco are one of five teams level on points at the top of the table as they were joined byParis FC, who edgedRennes4-3 thanks to Lassine Sinayoko’s injury-time penalty.Rennesdropped to fifth, a point behind, despite forward Estéban Lepaul’s hat-trick of penalties in Paris.Marseillepicked up a much-needed win as they thumpedAngers5-2 to pull away from the relegation zone.Le Havreremain rooted to the foot of the table as Cameroon forward Danny Namaso’s double helpedAuxerrecome away from Normandy with a 3-1 victory.View image in fullscreenKylian Mbappéblasts home Real Madrid’s third goal.Photograph: Ángel Martínez/Getty ImagesKylian Mbappé scored ⁠twice asRealMadridclosed the gap on ⁠La Liga leaders ⁠Barcelona ​to six points with a 4-1 home win over ⁠Sevillaon Sunday, a week ⁠before the rivals meet inel clásico.Arda Guler ​opened the ‌scoring in the ‌30th minute, arrowing a shot ‌into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappé added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappé ‌then won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute ​to effectively settle the contest.Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through the substitute Manu Bueno, ⁠but Yan Diomandé restored Real’s three-goal ​lead ​with a thunderous ​strike two minutes later.An early penalty from Ante Budimir and a late Asier Osambela goal from earnedOsasunaa 2-0 win againstRacing SantanderwhileCelta Vigowon 2-1 at home againstAlavés.Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick combined to score two goals asBayer Leverkusencame from behind to beat in-formFreiburg2-1 in the Bundesliga on Sunday.After a shock defeat to promoted Elversberg in the season opener, Leverkusen have now picked up 13 of a possible 18 points and sit fourth, level with third-placedFreiburg– who host Bayern Munich next weekend – on points.Rock bottomBorussia Mönchengladbachare still searching for a first point of the season after losing 2-1 at home against fellow strugglersHoffenheim.Hoffenheim’s Bambasé Conté opened the scoring with his second goal in two games since a surprise call-up to the Germany squad in October. Wael Mohya levelled for the hosts just after the break, but Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim back in front shortly afterwards as the visitors, who host Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, won just their second game of the season.View image in fullscreenPatrik Schick scores Bayer Leverkusen’s winner.Photograph: Martin Meissner/APLazio’s Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen ⁠scored in a 3-0 ⁠win over ​Juventuson Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter at the top of Serie A.Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the ⁠37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni’s cross afterLazioworked a short corner on the left.Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in ⁠the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Nuno Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto ​his left foot and bending a low ‌finish into the far ‌corner.Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counterattack from inside his own ‌half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered their side through to the final whistle.Cesc Fàbregas’sComoended their three-game winless streak in Serie A on Sunday with a 3-1 victory at lowlyFiorentina.First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put the visitors in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval. Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to put to bed any hope of a Fiorentina comeback and keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.Milanleapfrogged Como into fourth as they survived a second-half comeback fromAtalantato win 3-2. Goals from Gonçalo Ramos, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila put Milan 3-0 ahead after 58 minutes beforeAtalantarallied through Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic.Earlier,Leccewon 3-0 atUdinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N’Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballLigue 1BundesligaMonacoRennesParis FCLorientnewsShareReuse this content

title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter each scored twice in Chelsea’s 6-2 win as Tottenham conceded six for the second successive WSL game
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter each scored twice in Chelsea’s 6-2 win as Tottenham conceded six for the second successive WSL game
Content: Lauren James celebrates her second and Chelsea’s third at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLauren James celebrates her second and Chelsea’s third at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueJames and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL againSuzanne Wrackat Stamford BridgeSun 18 Oct 2026 09.13 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTwo goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.Chelsea 6-2 Tottenham: Women’s Super League – live reactionRead moreJames’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.View image in fullscreenLauren James squeezes in Chelsea’s opener from the tightest of angles.Photograph: John Walton/PAThe bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.Quick GuideWSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% recordShowManchester Cityheld off a spirited fightback fromBrightonto close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League.Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles.Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea.London City Lionessesmade it a full house for the top three, beatingEverton2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control.Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.Manchester Unitedare up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom sideCharlton3-1.Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark.Aston Villastunned falteringLiverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal.Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half asWest HamdefeatedCrystal Palace1-0.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFour minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.View image in fullscreenChelsea retake the lead in the second half thanks to Ellie Carpenter’s first goal.Photograph: John Walton/PA“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueChelsea WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Marcus Tavernier opened the scoring in the sixth minute as Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 to secure their first Premier League win of the season
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Marcus Tavernier opened the scoring in the sixth minute as Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 to secure their first Premier League win of the season
Content: Evanilson doubles Bournemouth’s lead after taking the ball past the Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEvanilson doubles Bournemouth’s lead after taking the ball past the Sunderland goalkeeper Robin Roefs.Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueEvanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man SunderlandJohn Brewinat the Vitality StadiumSun 18 Oct 2026 11.19 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 16.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for aPremier Leaguewin is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity,Sunderlandwere sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on CarrickRead moreThere was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched and their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.Both teams had made five changes from Thursday andBournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”Granit Xhaka’s early stumble prefaced a jet-lagged, error-strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away game since 1973. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home. “I was waiting for him to shoot but he can see more than you and me,” Rose said.“Exactly the situation we wanted to avoid,” Le Bris said, and Danso’s exit swiftly made things worse. Evanilson again escaped beyond a dallying defender exposed by Alderete ducking away from the ball. Clumsiness served as no defence. Craig Pawson, the referee, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel.View image in fullscreenMarcus Tavernier points the way after scoring Bournemouth’s first goal.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersBeing a goal and a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First‑half chances piled up, Robin Roefs repeatedly asked to bail out bungling defenders. “If you have one player more you have to use the momentum,” Rose said.With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris can only fight with the players available. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal following injury on international duty, was missing altogether from the matchday squad. “We decided not to rush the process,” Le Bris said. Timur Tutierov, loaned last season to Exeter, chased autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution on 59 minutes.On the sidelines Rose, who revealed last week that he had binge‑watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball. His need for three points was implicit. With the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands, relegation battles cannot be countenanced. The second goal was accompanied by a collective sigh of relief, arriving via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, assisted by Alderete’s brain-fog backpass, supplied a hip swivel of which Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud, sitting Roefs down to slot into an empty net. “I am happy that he rewarded himself with a goal,” Rose said of his No 9. “He is always working hard for the team.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenKevin Danso brings down Evanilson before being shown a red card by referee Craig Pawson.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersBournemouth signed off with 29 shots. If thoughts understandably drifted to Thursday and Milan, seven-time European champions, coming to Dorset, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted. Though Sunderland enjoyed a late, brief spell of pressure, Bournemouth calmly collected a win that capped a historic week in club history. “It felt very clear, after [the 5-1 defeat on Friday against] Chelsea we were waiting for this game,” Rose said. “I am settling in well, I love the region. It’s a pleasure to work here. Everyone here stays patient and I really appreciate it.”For Le Bris, any European success will only be a sticking plaster. “It’s hard to fix without a specific pattern,” he said, lamenting many mistakes. “It wasn’t the best version of Sunderland.”Two clubs facing similar challenges appear on different trajectories.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBournemouthSunderlandmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Osmand and Nygren at the double as Celtic thrash Hearts 7-1 | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Celtic moved four points clear of Rangers, who could only draw 2-2 with Dundee on Saturday, after a crushing 7-1 win against Hearts
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic moved four points clear of Rangers, who could only draw 2-2 with Dundee on Saturday, after a crushing 7-1 win against Hearts
Content: Benjamin Nygren is all smiles after scoring Celtic’s seventh goal against Hearts.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAView image in fullscreenBenjamin Nygren is all smiles after scoring Celtic’s seventh goal against Hearts.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Osmand and Nygren at the double as Celtic thrash Hearts 7-1Celtic move four points clear of Rangers after winRangers held to pulsating 2-2 draw against DundeePress AssociationSun 18 Oct 2026 12.15 EDTFirst published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 13.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCallum Osmand was on target again asCelticinflicted more misery onHeartswith a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.European football: Barcelona thrash Real Betis to maintain 100% recordRead moreThe Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear ofRangers.Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.Rangerspassed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw againstDundeeat Dens Park on Saturday. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point.View image in fullscreenBradley Fink gives Dundee the lead against Rangers from close range.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAGreg Kiltie scored twice to liftKilmarnockoff the bottom with a 3-2 home victory overMotherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFalkirksecured an entertaining 2-1 win atHibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell putFalkirk2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.Aberdeenreturned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory overSt Mirrenmoved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earnedDundee Uniteda 1-1 draw atSt Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipAberdeenSt MirrenHibernianFalkirkKilmarnockMotherwellnewsShareReuse this content

title: Martínez back ‘in a few weeks’ after jaw surgery; Liverpool lose Szoboszlai for ‘some time’ – matchday live | Soccer | The Guardian
description: All the latest on Sunday as there was positive news for Chelsea’s goalkeeper after surgery and bad news for Liverpool
Author: Rob Smyth
Headline: All the latest on Sunday as there was positive news for Chelsea’s goalkeeper after surgery and bad news for Liverpool
Content: 03.14 EDTMartinez back 'in a few weeks' after jaw surgeryChelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez said he would be fit to return “in a few weeks” following surgery on a fractured jaw sustained during his team’s 2-0 Premier League win at Everton.The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Martínez, 34, required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off on a stretcher. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso later said he had suffered a concussion.“Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well,” Martínez wrote on social media on Sunday alongside a photo of himself in a hospital bed. “The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.”Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. He joined from Belgian club Genk in August 2024 and has spent the past two seasons out on loan, including a spell at Strasbourg last term.Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injuryRead moreShareUpdated at08.35 EDT

title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One | Wigan Athletic | The Guardian
description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds
Author: Dominic Booth
Headline: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds
Content: Scott Hogan (left) with teammates after scoring the only goal of the game against Reading, which was Wigan’s first for 447 minutes in the leaguePhotograph: Harry McGuire/CameraSportView image in fullscreenScott Hogan (left) with teammates after scoring the only goal of the game against Reading, which was Wigan’s first for 447 minutes in the leaguePhotograph: Harry McGuire/CameraSportWigan AthleticWigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League OneGary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the cloudsDominic Boothat the Brick Community StadiumSun 18 Oct 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 11.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIf the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors,Wigan Athletic.Memories of thatfamous day at Wembleystill endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago.Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reelingRead moreThe club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell.Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction andrelegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted.The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996‑97 is a distinct possibility, although victory againstReading– the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier.“Some of our play was tremendous,” Caldwell said. “Our spirit, our character, our determination not to let the ball go in the net was fantastic. It was pretty stressful towards the end. We need to try and build on this. You have to keep the players believing and committing. There’s still so many aspects of our game that need to be better, but a result makes you feel better about yourself psychologically.”View image in fullscreenWigan fans cheer on their team during their win against Manchester City in the 2013 FA Cup final.Photograph: Shaun Botterill/Getty ImagesThe presence of Leam Richardson in the opposition dugout at the Brick Community Stadium gave fans more reason to reminisce about better days. Richardson, who claimed theLeague Onetitle as Wigan manager in April 2022, was sacked in November of the same year just 16 days after signing a three-year contract.Caldwell has also found himself under pressure. The former centre‑back has been criticised by fans for his team’s uninspiring style of play, which has produced just six goals in nine games, the fewest in League One. They went 447 minutes without a league goal until Hogan, the veteran forward, converted after Christian Saydee’s cross was parried out by the Reading goalkeeper, Joel Pereira.And while Wigan’s keeper, Joe Whitworth, was regularly called into action to see out the win, the home team were still good value for three points, allowing Caldwell and his squad to breathe. The manager’s backers will rightly point to the lack of spending by the club in the summer, with the £1.5m generated by the sale of Sam Tickle to Bristol City not yet reinvested on players and an overreliance on young loanees to prop up the squad.Danson and the club’s hierarchy have issued rallying cries to supporters to return to the stadium in an effort to generate more revenue, thus making the club more appealing to new owners, but why should fans part with hard‑earned cash to watch such insipid football?skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBefore the game, Caldwell said: “We also recognise the need for points is big, for our supporters to have that feelgood factor, and be able to leave the stadium in a much better frame of mind than they have been.”View image in fullscreenWigan’s Christian Saydee applauds the fans after the 1-0 win over Reading.Photograph: Harry McGuire/CameraSportThe Scot got what he needed against Reading, yet the sense of chaos above Caldwell was evidenced by the abrupt departure of Sarah Guilfoyle from her role as managing director on the eve of the new season, after a 10-year stay at the club. And there are plenty who feel the owners ought to bear the brunt of criticism.The Wigan Athletic Supporters Action Group is demanding answers from Danson on why selling the club has been such a struggle and the lack of investment. Other fans are more resigned to the idea that some short-term pain may be necessary for long-term gain; most agree a sale would be transformative.For now, despite a rare victory against a hitherto in-form Reading, the short-term struggles look likely to continue. The hope is that a hero of 2013 can perform miracles on the pitch, despite the constraints off it.Explore more on these topicsWigan AthleticLeague OneReadingfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘Like a fresh start’: Michael Carrick relieved by Manchester United’s draw at Leeds | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Manchester United’s head coach Michael Carrick claimed the 1-1 draw at Leeds ‘felt like a fresh start’ and insisted the season can still be a good one
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Manchester United’s head coach Michael Carrick claimed the 1-1 draw at Leeds ‘felt like a fresh start’ and insisted the season can still be a good one
Content: Michael Carrick applauds the Manchester United fans after the game at Elland Road.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick applauds the Manchester United fans after the game at Elland Road.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersManchester United‘Like a fresh start’: Michael Carrick relieved by Manchester United’s draw at LeedsHead coach insists ‘we can still have a really good season’‘We were the dominant side,’ says Leeds manager FarkeJamie Jacksonat Elland RoadSun 18 Oct 2026 12.50 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 14.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter a week in which Michael Carrick had “the headphones on” to quieten the noise, theManchester Unitedhead coach claimed his side’s 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday “felt like a fresh start” and insisted that the season can still be a good one.Carrick’s team have seven points from seven Premier League games and have won only once in the competition, against Ipswich in August. Sunday’s draw followed the previous weekend’s1-1 draw with Tottenham.Manchester United held as Calvert-Lewin’s Leeds leveller keeps pressure on CarrickRead moreYet after a week in which Unitedlost 2-0 at Atlético Madrid, after which Lisandro Martínez criticised the recruitment of the director of football, Jason Wilcox, Carrick was relieved at the point secured against Daniel Farke’s team.“[It’s been] quite quiet inside [the club] – the headphones have been on this week,” Carrick said. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start today – where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it. That didn’t surprise me today. We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end.“It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this club, because there was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days and they took it on the pitch. There was an edge to the game, an intensity. I spoke to the boys this morning about the history and what it means to the supporters, the club, to us coming over here into the territory.”Carrick admitted United’s league position is disappointing but he believes the club’s campaign can still be rescued. “If we keep doing the right things, we can still have a really good season. We’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that. But sometimes you do struggle.“We’ve got to find a way through it. We have to be stable enough to keep doing the right things and we’re more than capable of winning matches. I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I have no doubts that we can go on a good run. I’m encouraged by a lot of things.”Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half goal was cancelled out by Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s strike after the break, leaving Farke disappointed not to take all three points.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month that we were seen as favourites against Manchester United,” the Leeds manager said. “But we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right. We were the dominant side, but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box. It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective, but we have to keep going.”Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickLeeds UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: Kartal denied biggest win of career after Chwalinska fightback in Wuhan Open final | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal was denied her first major title after a 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 defeat by Maja Chwalinska in the final of the Wuhan Open in China
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Great Britain’s Sonay Kartal was denied her first major title after a 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 defeat by Maja Chwalinska in the final of the Wuhan Open in China
Content: Sonay Kartal will move into the world’s top 50 despite defeat in China.Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/ReutersView image in fullscreenSonay Kartal will move into the world’s top 50 despite defeat in China.Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/ReutersTennisKartal denied biggest win of career after Chwalinska fightback in Wuhan Open finalFrench Open finalist wins 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 for her first titleKartal will become new British No 1 after record runPress Association and Agence France-PresseSun 18 Oct 2026 09.51 EDTLast modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 12.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSonay Kartal missed out on winning the biggest title of her career as her brilliant run at the Wuhan Open ended in a final defeat by Maja Chwalinska.Kartal has enjoyed her best tournament only a fortnight after returning from six months out with a back injury, but her efforts appeared to catch up with her as she faded in a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 loss.Netball enters brave new world as New Zealand stun AustraliaRead moreInstead it was Chwalinska who lifted her first WTA 1000 trophy – the first of her career at any level on the WTA Tour – after fighting back from a set and a break down. The 25‑year‑old made a stunning breakthrough earlier this season when she reached the French Open final as a qualifier, and she will now move towards the top 10.At 170 in the world, Kartal wasthe lowest-ranked player to reach a finalat this level since the format was introduced in 2009 and only the second British woman after Johanna Konta. She fell short of matching Konta, who won the Miami Open in 2017, but Kartal’s reward will be a new ranking of 50, making her the British No 1 for the first time.“It was a very physical battle and I think I had my chances and I think that’s maybe where the rust of six months off comes in,” Kartal said. “But overall I’m very happy with my performance. Obviously not the result I wanted and it’s going to sting for a little while but I think for me the positives this week outweigh that result today. So I’m leaving here head high and in a good spot overall.”Kartal, whose only tour title came at a small event in Tunisia in 2024, continued the form she had shown throughout the tournament in the opening set, immediately breaking broke the relatively weak Chwalinska serve.The Pole possesses an unconventional game, relying more on the use of spins, slices and angles than pace, but two of Kartal’s greatest strengths are her patience and game intelligence, and she dealt with the challenge admirably. She put Chwalinska under constant pressure and broke serve twice more to clinch the opening set.Given her long break and the physical intensity of this run, it was perhaps not a surprise to see Kartal call the trainer at the end of the first set. She was given a pill, which she took after saving three break points in the opening game of the second set. Fatigue was starting to show and, after breaking serve to lead 2-0, Kartal was unable to battle through another long game.There was a delay after the second point of the fifth game when Chwalinska broke a shoelace chasing a wide ball but the Pole’s defensive skills were beginning to get the better of Kartal and the 16th seed made it one set all.Kartal tried to get back on the front foot at the start of the decider but she was constantly pushed back by high balls from her opponent and Chwalinska overcame late nerves to clinch victory.“[This title] tastes very sweet,” Chwalinska said. “I feel like I still don’t realise that I won. But it feels special, because after French Open, it was obviously amazing, but then I had some tough moments.“I feel like people also were very rough towards me. And it took a toll on me as well. I’m just a human. But I kept working really hard and I’m just very grateful that my work paid off.”Explore more on these topicsTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Netball enters brave new world as New Zealand stun Australia | Netball | The Guardian
description: New Zealand signalled their intent to set a new netball world order after stunning the Diamonds to kick off the Constellation Cup
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: New Zealand signalled their intent to set a new netball world order after stunning the Diamonds to kick off the Constellation Cup
Content: New Zealand players celebrate following their Constellation Cup win over Australia in Auckland.Photograph: Blake Armstrong/AAPView image in fullscreenNew Zealand players celebrate following their Constellation Cup win over Australia in Auckland.Photograph: Blake Armstrong/AAPNetballNetball enters brave new world as New Zealand stun AustraliaSilver Ferns win 56-50 to open Constellation Cup seriesGrace Nweke 40 from 41 against world No 1 DiamondsAustralian Associated PressSun 18 Oct 2026 06.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNew Zealand signalled their intent to set a new netball world order after stunning theDiamondsto kick off the Constellation Cup. The Commonwealth Games gold medallists picked up in Auckland where they left off in Glasgow with a 56-50 series-opening win at Spark Arena on Sunday.Experienced Diamonds duo Jo Weston (managed) and Kate Moloney (finger) were sorely missed by the world No 1 outfit, who were left in tears in Glasgow after settling for a bronze medal. Australia had suffered a shock semi-final defeat to Jamaica to miss a gold medal match for the first time since the sport joined the Games program in 1998.Diamonds netballer Sarah Klau named in Constellation Cup squad after pleading guilty to assaultRead moreFor so long second fiddle to the Diamonds, the Silver Ferns have the opportunity to disrupt netball’s status quo further ahead of next year’s World Cup. If they sweep the four-game trans-Tasman series, New Zealand will dethrone Australia for the world No 1 ranking for the first time since 2013.Diamonds coach Stacey Marinkovich admits Australia are still working on the heartbreak of their Glasgow campaign. “I don’t know if we were a bit tense coming in, but that’s the thing coming into New Zealand and off the loss of the Commonwealth Games,” Marinkovich said. “We just need to process that and work our way through what that experience was.”Grace Nweke was unconquerable on Sunday and fired off 40 goals from 41 attempts, spoiling Diamonds goalkeeper Courtney Bruce’s 100th game. New Zealand captain Karin Burger held up the other end with goalkeeper Kelly Jackson to shut down Australia’s full attacking roster of Kiera Austin, Sophie Garbin, Cara Koenen and Sophie Dwyer.The Silver Ferns charged to a 15-10 lead at quarter-time, thanks to a four-goal burst from Nweke. Marinkovich was forced to turn to her bench early, tasking debutant goalkeeper Jessie Grenvold with containing Nweke.The Diamonds coach also tweaked her attack, with Dwyer returning to the court for the first time since missing her after-the-siren shot against Jamaica. Goal attack Dwyer had been left unused on the bench in Australia’s bronze medal match win over England. New Zealand’s ascendancy continued well into the second quarter, soaring to a 10-goal lead after Nweke again fired off four straight goals.So uncharacteristic was the Diamonds’ performance that Marinkovich then took captain Liz Watson off the court, calling on Jamie-Lee Price to take centre duties for the second half. With Marinkovich’s bench depleted, the Diamonds came to life in the final quarter and scored 17 goals to New Zealand’s 11, but it was too little, too late.Marinkovich believes the Diamonds have been put on notice, with the Silver Ferns clearly benefiting from time spent in SuperNetball. “New Zealand are clinical at the moment,” Marinkovich said. “There’s no doubt that I think Super Netball has shown them what to do in pressured moments on a regular basis. Everyone’s capacities have certainly grown. That’s the reality of it now.”Explore more on these topicsNetballDiamondsNew Zealand netball teamAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: NFL today: How to watch Cowboys v Packers, TV channels & live stream Sunday 18 October | NFL | The Guardian
description: How will the Dallas and Green Bay fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options
Author: Alex Kirshner
Headline: How will the Dallas and Green Bay fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options
Content: Dak Prescott will hope to lead the Cowboys to victory on Sunday.Photograph: Ian Halperin/UPI/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenDak Prescott will hope to lead the Cowboys to victory on Sunday.Photograph: Ian Halperin/UPI/ShutterstockNFL watching and streaming guideNFLNFL today: How to watch Cowboys v Packers, TV channels & live stream Sunday 18 OctoberHow will the Dallas and Green Bay fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream optionsAlex KirshnerSun 18 Oct 2026 16.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Cowboys are trying to get off a treadmill on Sunday, having sequenced a loss, a win, a loss,a win, and then another loss through their first five games. Dallas’s magnetic attraction to staying within a game of .500 has so far not crushed them in the NFC East, where no team has more than three wins and the presumptive-favorite Eagles are floundering in the early season. It may well not take more than nine wins to claim the East this year, but the Cowboys have to start stacking them at some point.Their task Sunday in Green Bay will be a tough one. The Packers have had substantial injury problems but looked rejuvenated in putting a 31-7 beating on the Bears last week. While Chicago playing backup QBs Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum might explain their low point total, the Green Bay offenselooked like a revelation. Now the Pack get to face a Dallas defense that lost to a rookie QB 10 days ago and has yet to keep an opponent under 20 points. Can the Cowboys show some mettle on the road?Cowboys at PackersDate:Sunday 18 October 2026Time:8:20pm ET/5:20pm PT/1:20am BST (Monday)Stadium:Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin)How to watchUnited States:Watch on NBCor stream onFubo.Canada:Watch onTSN or CTV (RDS in French), or stream onFubo Sports Pro.United Kingdom:Watch onSky Sports NFL or Sky Sports Main Event, or stream withNOWorNFL Game Pass on DAZN.What to watch forThe Cowboys simply need to stop getting gashed in the run game. They’ve allowed a league-worst 168 rushing yards per game, a deficit that would surely keep them from containing even in a watered-down East if it held up much longer. The defense has also had problems containing the deep passing game, and that could be a particular problem against a Packers offense that is surging in that department. Christian Watson and Matthew Goldenbothhad 50-yard receptions from Jordan Love in a win over the Bears last week and combined for 266 yards. The Cowboys’ secondary, including newly acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr, have a serious task on their hands.The Packers will have their own challenges on defense, especially as they still await the return of star edge rusher (and scorned former Cowboy) Micah Parsons. The additional absences of front players Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave could mean a lot of time for Dak Prescott to forge connections with one of the sport’s top wideout tandems in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. There is a reason why the more gambling-inclined fans of the sport expect this to be the highest-scoring contest of the week (or at least tied with Raiders-Bills), with the teams pegged to combine for 50-some points.Explore more on these topicsNFLNFL watching and streaming guideDallas CowboysGreen Bay PackersUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

description: Lucia Di Guglielmo’s first NWSL goal sent Washington into the playoffs, while San Diego, Angel City and Kansas City also claimed victories on Saturday.
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lucia Di Guglielmo’s first NWSL goal sent Washington into the playoffs, while San Diego, Angel City and Kansas City also claimed victories on Saturday.
